body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT.

PR #2031 (BUG-1447) — APPROVED, and merged 36 seconds before my verdict landed. Not a problem
here, but worth naming because it is the second time today my verdict arrived after the merge.

    merged     21:19:23Z  as b09197ab72
    my verdict 21:19:59Z

The verdict agrees with the merge, so nothing is wrong with the outcome. What is worth noticing
is that it could equally have been a refusal, and nothing would have stopped the merge — I had
been reviewing for several minutes, the PR was CLEAN with no hold, and there is no signal that
says "a reviewer is currently looking at this". That is the same exposure as BUG-1490 seen from
the other end: there, a recorded refusal did not reach the readiness surface; here, a review IN
PROGRESS is invisible to anyone deciding to merge.

I am not filing it — an in-flight-review marker is a design question, not a defect, and
`aida session leases` already exists as a partial answer. But if either of you wants it as a
spec I have the timing evidence.

THE REVIEW ITSELF. All six acceptance criteria met, each verified rather than read, and I ran
the three named tests locally: 3 passed.

The thing worth saying, because it is the exact contrast with PR #2030 which I refused an hour
ago: the classification here is DERIVED in the test, not handed in.
`pr_2014_branch_policy_refusal_is_typed_with_clear_hint` calls the real
`classify_drain_merge_failure` with the verbatim PR-2014 error string and asserts the kind that
comes back is MergeHold, that it is not transient-retryable, and that the hint contains
`aida merge-hold clear 2014`. On #2030 the fixtures hand-wrote the artifact and asserted the
reader read it. Same author, same day, opposite test discipline — and it is the whole difference
between the two verdicts.

The mock-driver test DOES hand in FailureKind::MergeHold, which in isolation would be the #2030
gap. It is fine here only because the real-path test covers the classification separately, so
the chain is complete between them. Worth stating explicitly so nobody reads the mock test alone
and concludes the pattern is acceptable on its own.

ONE NON-BLOCKING FINDING, recorded because the spec predicted it. The fix takes the PROSE route,
not the typed one. The spec proposed classifying from `mergeStateStatus` (BLOCKED for policy vs
DIRTY for conflict) and allowed prose exclusion only "at minimum". So an upstream `gh` reword of
"the base branch policy prohibits the merge" silently returns this site to the broken behaviour
with no test of ours failing — which is precisely BUG-1435's shape, listed as Related on this
very spec, re-created at a new site. Within what the spec permitted, so I did not block; it
should be linked to BUG-1435 so the class is tracked rather than rediscovered an eighth time.

Mitigating, and the right call under the constraint: the new constant went into
aida-core/src/external_tool_output.rs — BUG-1310's inventory of external prose contracts —
rather than being inlined. The dependency is registered where the class is already tracked.
Hardcoding it in auto_complete.rs would have been materially worse for identical behaviour.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
